title: Remove the Phoenix connector
body:
Original scope and title of the issue: Figure out future for Phoenix connector

The connector continues to be hard to maintain. Specifically with the upgrade to Java 24 by March 2025 this is going to be tricky again. See #23498 

We will ask for community feedback about potential removal in the Trino Summit keynote and the following maintainer and contributor calls.

Potentially a hbase connector could also help but there is nothing happening on that front either and it might have similar technical challenges as well.

At this stage we might end up removing the connector unless we find contributors helping with it.

We will reach out to the Phoenix community again as well.


In the end the conclusion is the removal of the connector prior to our upgrade to Java 24 in March 2025. We are prepared to potentially take it back in when it supports the latest Java release as needed by Trino.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
What is the specific problem  with Phoenix and JDK24 ?

Is it SecurityManager and Subject.getSubject() related changes ?

There is a refection based worakround for those in Jetty that we can copy, but since most of that code is coming from Hadoop, it needs to be fixed there. 

Depending on the release schedules, March may not be a realistic deadline for that.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
CVEs is the main problem.
A secondary problem is use and presence of code which uses statics (Hadoop libraries) which causes issues with dynamic catalogs feature (cannot unload / load stuff like that safely without risk of leaking things).

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Are you using phoenix 5.2.1 ?

Phoenix 5.2.1 and the upcoming HBase 2.6.2 will work with the latest Hadoop 3.4.1 release.

There is a fair chance for HBase 2.6.2 to be released by next March.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Regarding the CVE issues:

The upcoming HBase 2.5 and 2.6 releases will include Hadoop 3.4.1, which is going to fix most of the CVEs.
We will also make a new Phoenix release that includes the CV fixed HBase releases.

The timeframe is a few months.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: I am more worried about Java 24 compatiblity, as that needs to be fixed in the whole stack, starting with Hadoop, which will take a long time to trickle up to Phoenix.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
From our interactions it looks like there is no immediate capability from the Phoenix and Hadoop community to make Phoenix work with Java 24 at this stage. Given that we are upgrading to Java 24 in March, we decided in the Trino Community Call on the 27th of Feb that we will remove the connector before the requirement change to Java 24.

Other projects can take up maintaining the connector or keep using older Trino release before the requirement change.

We are also prepared to take the connector back in once it supports whatever Java version is required by Trino at that stage. Trino will continue to move in sync with the Java releases.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Also in terms of the survey results there is very limited use of the Phoenix connector.

comments.author: reporter

Sorry for being late here, Lars brought the recent PR to my attention and I missed this whole conversation.
Isn't the problem with Java 24 compatibility in Hadoop stack causing any issue with Hive Connector? Does Hive (and any other Hadoop downstream) connector work with Java 24?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: The Hive connector does not depend on any Hive or Hadoop stuff .. we have clean implementations for all the file readers and object storage systems and so on.

comments.author: participant4

Sounds good, thanks!
Phoenix connector fails for Java 24 at compile time or runtime?
